title: Intel's 18A Client CPU Revenue Grows to Nearly One-Third of Segment Since Q1
summary:
Intel's first 18A-P client processor, Nova Lake, is tracking ahead of its development schedule, according to CEO Lip-Bu Tan. The company expects the new chip to secure double the design wins of the Panther Lake processor upon release and will share further specifications at CES in January. This product push follows a rapid ramp of the company's 18A node, with revenue from 18A client CPUs climbing from less than 5% in the first quarter to nearly one-third of the segment's total revenue today.

Tan reiterated his estimate that agentic AI workloads will expand the server CPU total addressable market to more than $200B within five years, noting that the ratio of CPUs to GPUs has shifted from 1-to-8 to 1-to-4 as AI agents require more code execution. He also confirmed that the Intel 14A node and the 18A-P process are both on track, with the latter scheduled for launch by the end of the year for several strategic external customers.
